entries.recording_review: Full Klemperer/New Philharmonia cast agrees with the documented 1965 EMI recording; eleven digital sections cover the five requested mass movements. Grouped movement timings agree with the LP within 3%.
limitations: Publisher/library documentation supports the recording family, not an exact barcode/take or Angel LP mastering guarantee.
Required named singers are supported within the contiguous work group; not every movement has every voice.

entries.recording_review: All thirteen requested Requiem sections and the Ancerl/Stader/Wagner/Haefliger/Borg/Czech Philharmonic cast agree with the documented 1959 recording; the different 1964 Ancerl cast is excluded.
limitations: Selected digital edition is a third-party reissue, not the original DG label; mastering, transfer provenance and exact take remain unverified.
Introitus/Kyrie corresponds to Requiem aeternam, Domine Jesu to Offertorium, and Sanctus/Benedictus to Sanctus; these mappings are restricted to this reviewed candidate.

entries.recording_review: All seven movements of Brahms Sonatas1/3 list both Gioconda de Vito and Edwin Fischer. Publisher/library documentation identifies their 1954 EMI recordings, consistent with the target pairing.
limitations: The original source heading repeats Op.78 and joins No.1 to the opus number. Reviewed as Sonata No.1, Op.78; the original Discogs text is retained.
BNF Collection digital transfer differs from the original EMI LP edition; exact transfer/mastering and take identity remain unverified.
